angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 234,451 km at 9.44 pc = 0.33 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 105.9789 +/- 0.0227 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 9.44 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.337 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 357 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract): 234,451 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.342 +/- 0.011 solar masses from Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 357 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3505 +/- 51 K from Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 357 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 357 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-357.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.917, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
